Purpose: Surface stakeholder needs before design begins
Inputs: stakeholder access, business objective stated by the sponsor, prior domain knowledge
Success: sponsor confirms requirement set represents intent

Purpose: give the organisation a shared model of the business it serves
Inputs: business documentation, stakeholder interviews, existing domain artefacts
Outputs: validated domain model, terminology, business rules
Success: domain experts ratify the model

Purpose: decompose and structure elicited requirements into a coherent set, resolving gaps and conflicts before modelling or validation begins
Inputs: the discovered business requirement set (#1's output), stakeholder context and constraints
Outputs: a structured, decomposed, categorised requirement set with gaps and conflicts identified and resolved or explicitly flagged
Service Level: completeness of decomposition, no unresolved conflict left silent, traceability from each detailed requirement back to its source statement, consistent categorisation
Governance: requirements-management policy, decomposition and traceability standard
Success: the analysed requirement set is accepted as ready for modelling (#4) or validation (#3) without needing further raw elicitation
Consumers: Modelling complex systems (#4), Validating engineering requirements (#3)

Purpose: confirm discovered requirements are correct, complete and agreed
Service Level: traceability, stakeholder sign-off, no unresolved conflict
Success: requirement baseline approved and frozen

Purpose: represent structural and behavioural complexity before committing to design
Success: model reviewed and accepted as basis for architecture

Purpose: evaluate proposed solutions for architectural integrity and organisational alignment
Inputs: approved solution proposal, business requirements, architectural constraint, applicable standard
Outputs: approved architectural decision, documented rationale, identified risk, recommendation
Service Level: compliance with architecture principle, complete reasoning, full traceability
Governance: enterprise architecture policy, security standard, technology standard, regulatory obligation
Success: decision approved, risk addressed, traceability established

Purpose: deliver a working component satisfying agreed expectation
Service Level: functional correctness, adherence to standard, maintainability
Success: component satisfies architectural and functional specification

Purpose: produce the detailed, element-level design of a specific component before construction begins
Inputs: architectural guidance and system-level structure (#5's output), analysed requirements (#58's output)
Outputs: a detailed design specification — module and class structure, interfaces, interaction and sequence design, data design, algorithm choice
Service Level: internal consistency, conformance to the architectural constraints it was handed, completeness (no significant design decision left for the developer to invent unspecified), testability of the resulting structure
Success: the design is accepted as ready for construction — a developer can implement against it without needing to make further design decisions

Purpose: preserve version integrity of every engineering artefact
Success: baseline reproducible on demand

Purpose: provide justified confidence the implementation satisfies specification
Inputs: implemented software, requirement baseline, test standard
Outputs: verification evidence, defect findings, confidence assessment
Success: confidence sufficient to justify release

Purpose: keep an accurate, current representation of engineering knowledge
Inputs: architectural decisions, implementation artefacts, requirement baseline
Success: documentation matches current system state

Purpose: identify and reduce exposure to security threat
Outputs: threat assessment, vulnerability findings, policy enforcement record
Success: no unmitigated critical vulnerability at release

Purpose: ensure engineering decisions comply with policy before taking effect
Success: decision recorded with traceable rationale

Purpose: determine and coordinate readiness for deployment
Success: release deployed without rollback

Purpose: keep deployed systems reliable and observable
Outputs: operational intelligence, incident records, performance data
Success: agreed availability target met

Purpose: reconstruct engineering understanding not currently captured
Inputs: legacy artefacts, historical decisions, source code
Success: recovered knowledge validated and published

Purpose: convert production experience into reusable understanding
Success: knowledge item published and referenced by future decisions

Purpose: keep engineering standards current with accumulated evidence
Inputs: evidence from service delivery, review findings
Success: revised standard formally published

Purpose: keep the capability portfolio aligned to shifting objectives
Inputs: revised or superseded Objectives, market/business signal
Success: capability portfolio reflects current Objectives

Purpose: maintain continuous, always-current architectural integrity assessment
Success: no undetected divergence exceeding tolerance

Purpose: keep documentation synchronised with current system state at all times
Success: no documentation ever found stale at audit

Purpose: keep every artefact relationship current without manual maintenance
Success: full trace path reconstructible on demand

Purpose: reconstruct disappeared engineering knowledge from legacy artefacts
Inputs: legacy code, historical records, operational history
Service Level: accuracy against ground truth where verifiable
Success: reconstructed knowledge validated by domain review

Purpose: evaluate every change against applicable policy the instant it occurs
Service Level: zero-lag detection, coverage of all applicable frameworks
Success: no compliance violation reaches release undetected

Purpose: keep every significant decision connected to its supporting evidence and outcome
Inputs: decision record, supporting evidence, governing policy
Success: any decision explainable on demand without reconstruction effort

Purpose: let engineering decisions emerge from accumulated organisational understanding rather than isolated discussion
Service Level: consistency with prior precedent, evidentiary support
Success: recommendation accepted or explicitly overridden with rationale

Purpose: keep the requirement baseline validated as it evolves, not only at baseline-freeze
Service Level: zero-lag detection of newly introduced conflict
Success: no invalid requirement reaches architecture undetected

Purpose: forecast engineering risk before it materialises
Inputs: historical risk/outcome data, current engineering state
Success: forecast risk actually materialising within predicted window, tracked

Purpose: maintain an always-current confidence assessment rather than a point-in-time one
Success: confidence score never stale at any release decision

Purpose: synthesise reusable understanding across every concurrent and historical project
Success: synthesised knowledge reused by at least one other project

Purpose: keep the capability-improvement loop running without waiting for retrospectives
Inputs: evidence generated by every service interaction
Service Level: cycle time between evidence and improvement
Success: measurable capability-maturity increase over time

Purpose: improve a capability's own effectiveness without waiting for external direction
Success: optimisation improves measured capability metric without introducing regression

Purpose: assess the consequence of a proposed change across the entire enterprise before it's made
Success: no unanticipated downstream impact discovered post-change

Purpose: keep requirement understanding synchronised with scattered, ongoing stakeholder signal
Success: no stale intent baseline older than defined threshold

Purpose: detect the moment the domain model diverges from actual business behaviour
Success: drift corrected before it propagates into requirements

Purpose: forecast when a pattern will fail to scale, before it breaks
Service Level: lead time before actual failure, accuracy
Success: forecast pattern replaced before failure occurs

Purpose: identify structural weakness in one system by reasoning across every system's architecture simultaneously
Success: pattern confirmed applicable and addressed

Purpose: propagate a fix or improvement to every place it applies, instantly
Success: all valid instances remediated

Purpose: verify deployed configuration matches declared intent at all times
Success: drift remediated before incident occurs

Purpose: identify defect classes current coverage would fail to catch, before they occur
Inputs: historical defect data, current test suite, architecture
Success: predicted gap closed before associated defect class occurs

Purpose: maintain whole-portfolio security exposure awareness continuously
Success: no critical exposure undetected between assessments (there are none — it's continuous)

Purpose: check the organisation's own exposure the moment a new attack pattern emerges elsewhere
Inputs: external threat intelligence, internal system inventory
Success: exposure checked and mitigated before exploitation

Purpose: detect latent contradiction across every active policy/standard/decision
Success: no unresolved conflict reaches enforcement

Purpose: maintain an ongoing, updating risk prediction for an in-progress release
Inputs: full history of prior release outcomes, current release content
Success: risk score correlates with actual post-release incident rate

Purpose: recognise precursor conditions of a future incident before it manifests
Success: anticipated incident prevented or mitigated pre-emptively

Purpose: reconstruct a full root-cause chain the instant an incident occurs
Success: root cause confirmed correct on human review

Purpose: draft or refine engineering standards directly from accumulating evidence
Inputs: evidence from service delivery across the organisation
Success: proposed revision formally adopted

Purpose: compare this organisation's capability maturity against every other capability instance the platform hosts
Success: benchmark-identified opportunity acted upon

Purpose: continuously check ongoing engineering work still serves its stated Objective
Success: drift corrected or Objective formally revised before divergence compounds

Purpose: determine the appropriate elicitation technique, deliverable set, and stakeholder-engagement plan for a given engagement before any elicitation begins
Inputs: the governing Objective's Statement, Template/commissioning context, stakeholder complexity, regulatory context
Outputs: a defined BA approach — selected techniques, deliverable set, governance checkpoints, stakeholder engagement plan
Service Level: fitness of approach to context (right-sized, neither over- nor under-specified for the engagement), completeness of governance checkpoints
Governance: organisational BA standard, Template's commissioning parameters
Success: approach approved by sponsoring authority before elicitation begins
Consumers: Discovering business requirements (#1), Understanding business domains (#2), Validating engineering requirements (#3)

Purpose: rank validated requirements by relative value, risk and dependency to guide delivery sequencing
Inputs: validated requirement baseline (output of #3), business value criteria, dependency graph, risk assessment
Service Level: consistent application of ranking criteria, documented rationale for every ranking, stakeholder agreement
Success: sponsor/product owner approves the ranked backlog
Consumers: Designing software architecture (#5, sequences design work), Constructing software systems (#6, sequences implementation), Managing software release (#12, sequences delivery)

Purpose: compare candidate solution options against the business need and recommend the one delivering the greatest net value
Inputs: validated requirement baseline, candidate solution options, cost/risk/value estimate for each option
Outputs: comparative option analysis, recommended solution with documented rationale
Service Level: completeness of options considered, transparency and defensibility of comparison criteria, full traceability from recommendation back to requirement
Governance: investment/procurement governance policy, architecture standard where options are technical
Success: sponsoring authority accepts the recommendation, or explicitly overrides it with documented rationale
Consumers: Designing software architecture (#5, receives the selected option as design input), Governing engineering decisions (#11, investment decision)

Purpose: combine separately constructed components into a coherent, working whole
Service Level: interface conformance, absence of integration defects, completeness
Success: integrated whole functions coherently and is accepted into system-level verification

Purpose: identify and leverage existing components, libraries or patterns instead of building from scratch
Outputs: identified reusable asset with fitness assessment
Service Level: fitness-for-purpose accuracy, security and quality vetting of the reused asset
Governance: reuse policy, licensing and security vetting standard
Success: reusable asset adopted in place of new construction, or explicitly rejected with documented rationale

Purpose: statically examine a completed artefact for defects and standard-conformance without executing it
Inputs: completed artefact (code or design), applicable standard/checklist
Outputs: review findings, approval or rejection decision
Service Level: coverage, reviewer independence from the artefact's producer, consistency of applied standard
Success: artefact approved for progression, or findings resolved and re-reviewed
Consumers: Constructing software systems (#6), Verifying software quality (#8)

Purpose: maintain a standing record of known-but-unresolved root causes and systematically eliminate them, independent of any single incident
Inputs: aggregated incident and root-cause history (#44), operational telemetry trend
Outputs: eliminated root causes, known-error record for those still open
Service Level: closure rate, recurrence rate after closure
Success: recurring root cause permanently eliminated, confirmed by absence of recurrence over a defined period
Consumers: Operating production systems (#13), Learning from operational experience (#15)

Purpose: track, triage, prioritise and close defects, functional and security, as a standing lifecycle
Inputs: defect findings (#8, #39), severity and impact criteria
Outputs: triaged and prioritised defect backlog, resolved and closed defects
Service Level: triage consistency, resolution timeliness relative to severity, no defect left untracked
Success: defect closed and verified resolved, or explicitly deferred with documented rationale and owner
Consumers: Constructing software systems (#6), Managing software release (#12, gated on defect status)

Purpose: formally manage relationships with external vendors, suppliers and service providers
Inputs: vendor/supplier candidates, contractual requirements, third-party risk criteria
Outputs: vendor contract, ongoing performance record, third-party risk assessment
Service Level: contract-compliance rate, vendor performance against SLA, completeness of risk assessment
Success: vendor relationship delivers contracted value within acceptable risk, or is terminated per policy
Consumers: Constructing software systems (#6, consumes vendor-supplied components), Protecting organisational assets (#10, needs third-party risk input)

Purpose: ensure a capability continues to serve the organisation effectively over time, distinct from exercising it day to day
Inputs: capability performance and telemetry data, evidence accumulated through service delivery (the Capability→Service→Evidence→Knowledge loop, Ch.7 §7.10), the current Objective set defining what capability the organisation actually needs, the existing capability portfolio
Outputs: capability maturity assessment, identified capability gaps, capability metrics, a coordinated evolution roadmap
Service Level: the five dimensions §6.13 names for capability measurement itself — outcome consistency, resilience, adaptability, organisational learning, alignment with organisational objective
Governance: capability-ownership mandate, strategic-governance policy — explicitly not line-management authority (§6.11: "should not be confused with traditional line management")
Success: measurable increase in capability maturity over time, and every identified gap either addressed or explicitly accepted as strategic debt with a named owner
Consumers: Governing engineering decisions (#11), Adapting to changing business need (#17), and every capability whose maturity is being assessed

Purpose: evaluate, approve, schedule and coordinate a proposed change based on its risk and potential conflict with other concurrent changes
Inputs: the change request, the current schedule of other approved or pending changes, risk-classification criteria
Outputs: an approved, rejected, or rescheduled change decision, with a conflict assessment against other in-flight changes
Service Level: consistency of risk assessment across similar changes, accuracy of conflict detection (no two conflicting changes approved into the same window), decision timeliness relative to the change's urgency
Success: the change proceeds without causing an avoidable conflict or incident, or is correctly rejected or rescheduled before it can
Consumers: Managing engineering configuration (#7, records the approved change into the baseline), Constructing software systems (#6, implements it), Managing software release (#12, release scheduling depends on which changes have cleared)
